reading: A grid is cut by separator lines with noise in the cells. Four separator crossings show the background colour instead of the line colour; the output is the box with those four cells as corners, cut from the input.

new_rows.name: gap_corner
new_rows.datalog:
fgc(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
bgc(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !fgc(Y, X).
gap_corner(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), X1 = X - 1, X2 = X + 1, Y1 = Y - 1, Y2 = Y + 1, cell(Y, X1, S), cell(Y, X2, S), cell(Y1, X, S), cell(Y2, X, S).

why: exactly four background cells have all four orthogonal neighbours in one separator colour; the output equals the input box spanned by them
invariants: output cells are copied unchanged from the input

reading: The 8 shape moves down one row and is recoloured to 2.
why: output shape equals input shape shifted by (+1,0), colour 8 becomes 2

reading: Each 5x5 room of 0 inside the 8 background has a 3x3 centre. Every 0 cell of that centre takes the digit at the same position of a fixed keypad [[1,7,6],[4,0,5],[2,9,3]]; its 8 cells stay 8.

slots.room: each 0 region bounded by 8 whose ring is a 1-cell 0 margin around a 3x3 centre
slots.mask: only 0 cells of the centre are written; 8 cells kept

why: every changed cell is a 0 cell in a room centre, and its new colour is the keypad digit at its relative position

reading: Each row has one 5; the whole row is painted a colour chosen by the 5's column: left 2, middle 4, right 3.
why: every output row is uniform, coloured by the column index of that row's 5

reading: Scattered 3x3 pieces (grey 5 with a coloured edge part) are assembled into a 9x9 square: each piece goes to the slot (corner, edge or centre) where its coloured part lies on the outer rim.

slots.pieces: the nine 3x3 blocks made of 5 and one other colour (one all 5)
slots.slot: the 3x3 position in the 9x9 output whose outer side matches where the piece's coloured cells are
slots.output: 9x9 grid of the pieces placed unchanged

why: every 3x3 block of the output is one input piece copied unchanged, and the coloured cells all lie on the outer rim
invariants: piece contents are not rotated or recoloured

reading: Rectangles of 0 at least 2x2 are filled with 2. Take the maximal all-0 rectangles; a rectangle that overlaps a strictly larger one is skipped.

new_rows.name: zero_rect
new_rows.datalog:
zero(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0).
nz(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C != 0.
cand(Y0, X0, Y1, X1) :- zero(Y0, X0), zero(Y1, X1), Y1 > Y0, X1 > X0.
bad(Y0, X0, Y1, X1) :- cand(Y0, X0, Y1, X1), nz(Y, X), Y >= Y0, Y <= Y1, X >= X0, X <= X1.
rect(Y0, X0, Y1, X1) :- cand(Y0, X0, Y1, X1), !bad(Y0, X0, Y1, X1).
grow(Y0, X0, Y1, X1) :- rect(Y0, X0, Y1, X1), A = Y0 - 1, rect(A, X0, Y1, X1).
grow(Y0, X0, Y1, X1) :- rect(Y0, X0, Y1, X1), A = X0 - 1, rect(Y0, A, Y1, X1).
grow(Y0, X0, Y1, X1) :- rect(Y0, X0, Y1, X1), A = Y1 + 1, rect(Y0, X0, A, X1).
grow(Y0, X0, Y1, X1) :- rect(Y0, X0, Y1, X1), A = X1 + 1, rect(Y0, X0, Y1, A).
mrect(Y0, X0, Y1, X1) :- rect(Y0, X0, Y1, X1), !grow(Y0, X0, Y1, X1).
marea(Y0, X0, Y1, X1, A) :- mrect(Y0, X0, Y1, X1), H0 = Y1 - Y0, H = H0 + 1, W0 = X1 - X0, W = W0 + 1, A = H * W.
dom(Y0, X0, Y1, X1) :- marea(Y0, X0, Y1, X1, A), marea(P0, Q0, P1, Q1, B), B > A, P0 <= Y1, Y0 <= P1, Q0 <= X1, X0 <= Q1.
keep(Y0, X0, Y1, X1) :- mrect(Y0, X0, Y1, X1), !dom(Y0, X0, Y1, X1).
zero_rect(Y, X) :- keep(Y0, X0, Y1, X1), zero(Y, X), Y >= Y0, Y <= Y1, X >= X0, X <= X1.

why: the changed cells are exactly the 0 cells of maximal all-0 rectangles (at least 2x2) that overlap no larger such rectangle; all become 2

reading: The single 2 is removed and its four diagonal neighbours get fixed colours: up-left 3, up-right 6, down-left 8, down-right 7 (clipped at the border).
why: the output is the 3x3 pattern [[3,0,6],[0,0,0],[8,0,7]] centred on the marker, clipped to the grid

reading: In the 0 room inside the 5 walls, an 8 diagonal is drawn from a top corner pocket (wall above and wall behind it). The diagonal chosen is the longest run of 0 cells.

new_rows.name: corner_diag
new_rows.datalog:
zero(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0).
wall(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C != 0.
ra(Y0, X0, Y0, X0) :- zero(Y0, X0), Y1 = Y0 - 1, X1 = X0 - 1, wall(Y1, X0), wall(Y0, X1).
ra(Y0, X0, Y2, X2) :- ra(Y0, X0, Y, X), Y2 = Y + 1, X2 = X + 1, zero(Y2, X2).
rb(Y0, X0, Y0, X0) :- zero(Y0, X0), Y1 = Y0 - 1, X1 = X0 + 1, wall(Y1, X0), wall(Y0, X1).
rb(Y0, X0, Y2, X2) :- rb(Y0, X0, Y, X), Y2 = Y + 1, X2 = X - 1, zero(Y2, X2).
la(Y0, X0, count(Y, X)) :- ra(Y0, X0, Y, X).
lb(Y0, X0, count(Y, X)) :- rb(Y0, X0, Y, X).
len(N) :- la(Y0, X0, N).
len(N) :- lb(Y0, X0, N).
best(max(N)) :- len(N).
corner_diag(Y, X) :- la(Y0, X0, N), best(N), ra(Y0, X0, Y, X).
corner_diag(Y, X) :- lb(Y0, X0, N), best(N), rb(Y0, X0, Y, X).

why: the 8 cells are exactly the longest diagonal 0-run that starts at a top corner pocket; nothing else changes

reading: Pairs of 2x2 8-blocks sit on the same two rows like brackets. The 2-row strip between each pair is cut out, and the strips are stacked top to bottom.

slots.brackets: 2x2 blocks of 8, paired by sharing the same rows
slots.strip: the cells strictly between a pair, on those two rows
slots.order: strips stacked by row, top to bottom
slots.output: the vertical stack of strips (all same width)

why: every output row pair equals the cells between one bracket pair, in top-to-bottom order

reading: Count the 8-connected objects of each colour on the 7 background. Draw a bottom-aligned bar chart with fixed column order 5,2,8,9,6, each bar as tall as its colour's object count, on 7.

slots.count: number of 8-connected objects of each colour
slots.columns: fixed colour order [5,2,8,9,6] (learned from training), width 5
slots.height: max count; bars grow up from the bottom row

why: output column j holds colour order[j] in its bottom count(order[j]) cells and 7 above
